items.readable_text:
Content:
When simplifying expressions containing [MATH: \cot] and [MATH: \csc,] we can use the following cotangent-cosecant identity:

Content:
[MATH: 1 + \cot^2 x= \csc^2 x]

Content:
The identity above can be obtained by starting with the Pythagorean identity:

Content:
[MATH: \sin^{2} x + \cos^{2} x = 1]

Content:
We divide both sides by [MATH: \color{black}\sin^2 x] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (\sin^{2} x)/(\sin^{2} x) + (\cos^{2} x)/(\sin^{2} x)|= (1)/(\sin^{2} x)]

Content:
Simplifying the above using [MATH: \cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}] and [MATH: \csc x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x}] gives

Content:
[MATH: 1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x,]

Content:
as required.

sections.normalized_html:
First, using the identity [MATH: 1 + \cot^2 \theta = \csc^2 \theta,] we rewrite the expression in the parentheses:

[MATH: \sin θ(1 + \cot^{2} θ) = \sin θ ⋅ \csc^{2} θ]

Then, using the fact that [MATH: \csc {\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin{\theta}},] we can further simplify the expression:

[MATH: \sin θ ⋅ \csc^{2} θ|= \sin θ ⋅ (1)/(\sin^{2} θ); = \sin θ ⋅ (1)/(\sin θ ⋅ \sin θ); = (1)/(\sin θ); = \csc θ]

Content:
If we subtract [MATH: 1] from both sides of the cotangent-cosecant identity [MATH: 1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta,] we get

Content:
[MATH: \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta - 1.]

Content:
This is an alternate form of the cotangent-cosecant identity.

Content:
We can also get a second alternate form if we start with [MATH: 1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta] and subtract [MATH: \cot^2\theta] from both sides. This gives

Content:
[MATH: \csc^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When simplifying expressions containing [MATH: \cot] and [MATH: \csc,] we can use the following cotangent-cosecant identity:

Content:
[MATH: 1 + \cot^2 x= \csc^2 x]

Content:
The identity above can be obtained by starting with the Pythagorean identity:

Content:
[MATH: \sin^{2} x + \cos^{2} x = 1]

Content:
We divide both sides by [MATH: \color{black}\sin^2 x] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: (\sin^{2} x)/(\sin^{2} x) + (\cos^{2} x)/(\sin^{2} x)|= (1)/(\sin^{2} x)]

Content:
Simplifying the above using [MATH: \cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}] and [MATH: \csc x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x}] gives

Content:
[MATH: 1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x,]

Content:
as required.

---

Item 2 — Example: Simplifying an Expression Using the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity

Example Prompt:
Simplify the trigonometric expression [MATH: \sin \theta \, (1 + \cot^2 \theta)].

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, using the identity [MATH: 1 + \cot^2 \theta = \csc^2 \theta,] we rewrite the expression in the parentheses:

[MATH: \sin θ(1 + \cot^{2} θ) = \sin θ ⋅ \csc^{2} θ]

Then, using the fact that [MATH: \csc {\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\sin{\theta}},] we can further simplify the expression:

[MATH: \sin θ ⋅ \csc^{2} θ|= \sin θ ⋅ (1)/(\sin^{2} θ); = \sin θ ⋅ (1)/(\sin θ ⋅ \sin θ); = (1)/(\sin θ); = \csc θ]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity

Content:
If we subtract [MATH: 1] from both sides of the cotangent-cosecant identity [MATH: 1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta,] we get

Content:
[MATH: \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta - 1.]

Content:
This is an alternate form of the cotangent-cosecant identity.

Content:
We can also get a second alternate form if we start with [MATH: 1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta] and subtract [MATH: \cot^2\theta] from both sides. This gives

Content:
[MATH: \csc^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1.]

Item 9 — Example: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using Various Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity

Explanation:
First, we factor [MATH: \csc x] from the first two terms, as follows:

[MATH: \csc x + \csc x\cot^{2} x − \csc^{3} x|= \csc x(1 + \cot^{2} x) − \csc^{3} x]

Now, using the cotangent-cosecant identity,
[MATH: 1+ \cot^2 x=\csc^2 x ,]
we get

[MATH: \csc x(1 + \cot^{2} x) − \csc^{3} x|= \csc x ⋅ (\csc^{2} x) − \csc^{3} x; = \csc^{3} x − \csc^{3} x; = 0.]

Item 12 — Example: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity

Content:

Explanation:
First, we recall the following identity:
[MATH: 1= \csc^2{\theta} -\cot^2{\theta}]

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

[MATH: (1)/(\csc θ + \cot θ) + \cot θ|= (\csc^{2} θ − \cot^{2} θ)/(\csc θ + \cot θ) + \cot θ; = ((\csc θ − \cot θ)(\csc θ + \cot θ))/(\csc θ + \cot θ) + \cot θ; = ((\csc θ − \cot θ)(\csc θ + \cot θ))/(\csc θ + \cot θ) + \cot θ; = (\csc θ − \cot θ) + \cot θ; = \csc θ.]
